_doc: #741 ONE RESOLVER FOR THE FLEET, enforced. The SuperApp's Configs > Mesh > DNS page decides where every name the phone looks up is answered (applied at its VPN by firestack; 'Mirror Android' passes through to Private DNS). An app inherits that choice only while it asks Android's resolver; a public server written into code, a resolv.conf naming one, a DNS-over-HTTPS client or a raw socket to :53 each answer from somewhere the menu never sees. 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-dns-resolver-guard.py reads every tracked file under the fleet's app and library trees and fails on any of the patterns below outside the two places allowed to talk DNS at all. Read by the guard and by its tester; nothing in either names a server or a path on its own.
_doc_scan: Path prefixes of the fleet's own trees (apps, libraries, engines, terminal rootfs declarations). 1_cicd is not scanned: it is where this guard and its fixtures live.
_doc_skip: Never read: build outputs, vendored dependency trees and binary or lock files, which are not code the fleet writes.
_doc_rules: Each rule is a regular expression applied per line, optionally only to files with the listed suffixes; needles are plain substrings at least one of which every match contains, so a file holding none of them is never read line by line (the whole fleet is scanned on every push). public-dns-ip lists the public resolvers an app could pin; resolv-nameserver catches any resolv.conf line naming something other than the loopback bridge (libs/sysdns), which is also how a mesh resolver hardcoded per app shows up; the rest are the ways code brings its own resolver.

public-dns-ip.why: a public DNS server written into the fleet's code: lookups through it skip the SuperApp's DNS menu

resolv-nameserver.why: a resolv.conf naming a server other than 127.0.0.1, the loopback bridge to Android's resolver (libs/sysdns)

nameservers-list.why: a declared nameservers list (a rootfs.json or build.json a build script writes resolv.conf from) naming a server other than the loopback bridge: the nameserver prefix is only added at build time, so resolv-nameserver never sees it

custom-resolver-lib.why: a resolver library of the app's own (DoH client, dnsjava, minidns, hickory/trust-dns): it answers from its own upstream, not Android's

custom-okhttp-dns.why: an OkHttp Dns of the app's own instead of Dns.SYSTEM

doh-endpoint.why: a DNS-over-HTTPS endpoint: lookups sent there never reach Android's resolver

raw-dns-port.why: a socket aimed at port 53: a hand-rolled DNS client

_doc_allow: The ONLY trees allowed to name servers or speak DNS, each with the reason. Everything else that matches a rule is a failure.

allow.aa_cloud-superapp/: The SuperApp IS the fleet's DNS layer: its VPN, the WireGuard profiles' DNS lines and the Configs > Mesh > DNS presets (#740) are where upstream servers, including the mesh resolver for the split-DNS rule, are declared once for every app.
allow.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/firewall/: firestack, the engine the SuperApp's VPN runs: its DNS transports (DoH, DoT, dns53) are how the menu's choice is applied.
allow.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/sysdns/: The shared shim (#741) that bridges bundled binaries and terminal shells to Android's resolver.
allow.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/appstore/: #899 (owner's rule, 2026-10-07): the Store's download hosts only (StoreDns.isStoreHost), and ONLY after the fleet bridge (which walks the DNS menu's preset) and Android's own resolver both declined. A direct DoH query by IP is the third rung of the Store's ladder (DnsLadder), never the first, and every rung asked is named in the failed row's error.

_doc_probe: #758 the on-device half of this guard. Static rules can only say no code here brings its own resolver; whether the menu's choice actually reaches an app is read on the phone, from that app's own process, through the debug API every app gets from libs:devtools (linked by libs:core). AppDebugServer serves GET /api/net/dns (the default network for the app's uid, VPN or not, its DNS servers = the menu's upstreams under the SuperApp's VPN, Private DNS state) and GET /api/net/resolve?host= (Android's answer for that uid). Each entry is a file and the texts it must keep holding; losing one fails the guard, so the probe cannot be deleted or quietly turned into a second resolver (it must resolve with InetAddress, which is Android's).
_doc_exempt: Single literals in vendored or unrelated code that match a rule but are not a DNS server, pinned to the file AND the text: the same file gaining any other match still fails.

exempt.reason: A comment explaining an IPv6-only carrier, not a lookup.
